title: Financial Frequency Combs
authors: Madhurendra Mishra, Armaan Aryan, Arsh Gogia, Adarsh Ganesan
abstract: Frequency combs are discrete, equally spaced, phase-coherent spectral lines that emerge from nonlinear mode coupling in physical systems. We show that the incommensurate fractional-order financial model of Huang, Li, Ma, and Chen, whose Caputo derivatives encode macroeconomic long-range memory, generates an analogous structure in its steady-state spectrum. The comb appears only over specific values and ranges of the saving amount $a$, the investment cost $b$, and the demand elasticity $c$, outside which the spectral lines lose their equal spacing. It persists across extended parameter regimes and stays invariant to perturbations in the initial interest rate $x_0$ and investment demand $y_0$, while distinct spectral regimes appear at different initial price levels $z_0$. The comb is generated only when the fractional-order exponents $q_1$, $q_2$, and $q_3$ associated with interest rate, investment demand, and price index are above the critical threshold values. At even higher values of these exponents, the frequency comb transitions into chaos. These findings show that the long-run cyclic structure of a memory-bearing financial economy organises into a discrete, deterministic spectral fingerprint rather than a stochastic continuum.
summary: This work applies nonlinear dynamics and fractional calculus to a financial model to test if long-memory economic fluctuations exhibit a predictable, discrete spectral fingerprint called a frequency comb. The results show that such a deterministic structure emerges only when specific parameters and fractional exponents fall within narrow, stable regimes. This suggests a profound link between memory effects in finance and underlying harmonic organization.
main_problem: The study investigates whether long-range memory financial systems can exhibit a deterministic, discrete spectral fingerprint analogous to a frequency comb.
main_result: Under specific parameter and fractional-order conditions, the system's steady-state power spectrum organizes into a clear, equidistant frequency comb structure. This suggests that complex economic cycles might possess an underlying deterministic periodicity rather than being purely stochastic.
method: The authors employed numerical integration of a nonlinear, fractional-order financial model followed by Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) spectral analysis to diagnose the presence and stability of the comb.
model_or_system: The system is based on a three-dimensional nonlinear financial model involving interest rate ($x$), investment demand ($y$), and price index ($z$). This model is generalized using Caputo fractional derivatives ($	ext{D}^{q_i}$) to incorporate long-range memory effects into the dynamics.
key_observables: The primary observable is the power spectrum, specifically looking for discrete, equally spaced spectral lines (the frequency comb). Other observables include Lyapunov exponents and phase portrait geometry.
important_parameters: Structural parameters include saving amount ($a$), investment cost ($b$), and demand elasticity ($c$). Crucially, the fractional orders ($q_1, q_2, q_3$) dictate whether the comb appears or if the system transitions to chaos.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed spectral structure is governed by a single bounded, two-lobed motion in the phase space. The use of the Caputo fractional derivative formulation is central to the model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate time series, FFT spectra showing the comb under varying parameters ($a, b, c$), and how the comb's existence depends on the specific ranges of the fractional orders ($q_1, q_2, q_3$).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the nonlinear financial model, generalizing it to fractional order dynamics, performing extensive parameter sweeps across structural constants ($a, b, c$) and memory exponents ($q_i$), and analyzing the resulting spectral signatures.
why_interesting: While not directly quantum, the mathematical framework of using fractional calculus and spectral analysis to characterize deterministic structure in complex systems mirrors techniques used in open quantum systems modeling or characterizing non-Markovian dynamics where long-term memory effects are crucial.
